explanation: Well-formedness is about the model being properly named, identified, and structured. High fidelity is about accurately reflecting the real context, including constraints and exceptions. If the diagram is clear but misses a rule about mandatory assignment to one carrier, it can still be well-formed while falling short on fidelity.

options.text: It is well-formed but not fully high-fidelity because a relevant business constraint is missing.
It is high-fidelity but not well-formed because constraints are part of naming.
It is neither well-formed nor high-fidelity because every missing rule makes the diagram invalid.
It is complete because identifiers matter more than constraints.

prompt: A team presents a data model that uses clear entity names and identifiers, but it omits a rule that a shipment must belong to exactly one carrier. How should the model be judged?
